### Obesity-attributable QALY loss

QALYs lost to high BMI are the absolute utility decrement from Carrello et al. [@Carrello2021] for each person's BMI category, times their survey weight and person-years (`qaly_loss_weighted`, undiscounted; deaths count half a year). Obesity-attributable loss sums obesity classes I to III; high-BMI loss also includes overweight. Totals are computed within each simulation replication, then summarised as the mean and 95% simulation interval (2.5th and 97.5th percentiles). Rates are per 100,000 adult person-years.

```{r}
#| label: build-qaly-loss

summarise_qaly_loss <- function(individual, loss_categories) {
  individual |>
    dplyr::summarise(
      qaly_loss = sum(
        qaly_loss_weighted[bmi_category %in% loss_categories],
        na.rm = TRUE
      ),
      person_years = sum(survey_weight * person_years, na.rm = TRUE),
      .by = c(simulation, year, sex)
    ) |>
    dplyr::mutate(qaly_loss_per100k = 1e5 * qaly_loss / person_years) |>
    dplyr::summarise(
      qaly_loss_mean         = mean(qaly_loss),
      qaly_loss_lo           = stats::quantile(qaly_loss, 0.025, names = FALSE),
      qaly_loss_hi           = stats::quantile(qaly_loss, 0.975, names = FALSE),
      qaly_loss_per100k_mean = mean(qaly_loss_per100k),
      qaly_loss_per100k_lo   = stats::quantile(qaly_loss_per100k, 0.025, names = FALSE),
      qaly_loss_per100k_hi   = stats::quantile(qaly_loss_per100k, 0.975, names = FALSE),
      .by = c(year, sex)
    ) |>
    dplyr::arrange(year, sex)
}

obesity_categories  <- c("obesity_I", "obesity_II", "obesity_III")
high_bmi_categories <- c("overweight", obesity_categories)

qaly_loss_by_year_sex <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  summarise_qaly_loss(qaly_results$individual, obesity_categories) |>
    dplyr::mutate(exposure = "Obesity (BMI >= 30)", .before = 1L),
  summarise_qaly_loss(qaly_results$individual, high_bmi_categories) |>
    dplyr::mutate(exposure = "High BMI (BMI >= 25)", .before = 1L)
)

write_result_csv(
  qaly_loss_by_year_sex,
  "module2_qaly_loss_obesity_high_bmi_by_year_sex.csv"
)
```

#### Sensitivity to the BMI utility decrements

The obesity-attributable QALY loss is recalculated with every BMI utility decrement set to the lower and then the upper bound of its Carrello et al. 95% confidence interval.

```{r}
#| label: run-qaly-decrement-sensitivity
#| cache: false

qaly_decrement_scenarios <- list(
  "Lower 95% CI decrements" = c(
    overweight = -0.010, obesity_I = -0.017,
    obesity_II = -0.028, obesity_III = -0.039
  ),
  "Upper 95% CI decrements" = c(
    overweight = -0.030, obesity_I = -0.077,
    obesity_II = -0.116, obesity_III = -0.130
  )
)

# The two scenario QALY runs take about two hours with 50 replications, so
# their summary is cached next to the simulation file. Delete this file if
# the simulation, the decrements or the QALY code change.
qaly_decrement_cache_file <- file.path(
  results_dir,
  paste0(
    "module2_qaly_decrement_sensitivity_", simulation_version,
    "_nsim", n_simulations_main, ".rds"
  )
)

if (file.exists(qaly_decrement_cache_file)) {
  qaly_decrement_sensitivity <- readRDS(qaly_decrement_cache_file)
} else {
qaly_decrement_sensitivity <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  summarise_qaly_loss(qaly_results$individual, obesity_categories) |>
    dplyr::mutate(scenario = "Base case decrements", .before = 1L),
  lapply(names(qaly_decrement_scenarios), function(scenario_name) {
    scenario_qalys <- simeq_calculate_qalys(
      simulation_output = simulation_historical,
      min_age = 20L,
      max_age = 84L,
      reference_bmi_prevalence = reference_bmi_prevalence,
      bmi_decrements = qaly_decrement_scenarios[[scenario_name]]
    )
    summarise_qaly_loss(scenario_qalys$individual, obesity_categories) |>
      dplyr::mutate(scenario = scenario_name, .before = 1L)
  })
) |>
  dplyr::filter(year %in% reported_years)
saveRDS(qaly_decrement_sensitivity, qaly_decrement_cache_file)
}

write_result_csv(
  qaly_decrement_sensitivity,
  "module2_qaly_loss_obesity_decrement_sensitivity.csv"
)
```

### Obesity-attributable years of life lost {#sec-yll}

This section treats the simulation as a **prevalence projection tool**: simulated annual BMI-category prevalence is used as the time-varying exposure input to an external burden calculation, following the same logic as the cost module (@sec-module3). Up to 2024, the simulation's mortality is recalibrated to each year's Portuguese life table within each age-sex stratum, so total simulated deaths track the life table regardless of BMI composition. From 2025 the calibration is held at its 2024 values and baseline mortality follows the Lee-Carter projected life tables, so projected deaths respond to changes in the BMI and education distribution as well as to the projected decline in mortality. The estimates are anchored to life-table-consistent mortality, not to a simulation counterfactual.

Module 2 reports two obesity-attributable measures: the QALY loss (@sec-qaly) and years of life lost. DALYs are not reported, because a years-lived-with-disability component built from the same BMI utility decrements would duplicate the QALY loss.

**Population-attributable fraction (PAF)** — obesity classes I, II, and III are the exposed categories ($c$), each with simulated annual prevalence $p_c$ and all-cause mortality relative risk $RR_c$ versus normal weight [@DiAngelantonio2016]. Overweight and underweight contribute zero to the PAF:

$$PAF = \frac{\displaystyle\sum_c p_c \,(RR_c - 1)}{1 + \displaystyle\sum_c p_c \,(RR_c - 1)}$$

Deaths occurring between year $t-1$ and year $t$ are attributed using the PAF from year $t-1$, when the BMI that exposed them was measured.

**Years of life lost (YLL)** — for each simulated death at age $a_i$ in sex $s$, YLL is the remaining life expectancy $e_s(a_i)$ at that age and sex from the 2019 Portuguese life table:

$$YLL_i = e_s(a_i)$$

Obesity-attributable YLL is obtained by applying the PAF to life-table-consistent total YLL:

$$YLL_{\text{attrib}} = YLL_{\text{total}} \times PAF$$

Obesity-attributable YLL is expressed per 100,000 simulated adults. It is a population-level projection and is not directly comparable to disease-specific GBD estimates or to Borges et al. (2025).

```{r}
#| label: run-module2-yll
#| cache: false

yll_results <- simeq_calculate_yll(
  simulation_output = simulation_historical,
  ref_life_expectancy = ref_life_expectancy,
  min_age           = 20L,
  max_age           = 84L
)

write_result_csv(yll_results$by_year,  "module2_yll_by_year.csv")
write_result_csv(yll_results$overall,  "module2_yll_overall.csv")
```

## Module 3: High-BMI-Attributable Costs {#sec-module3}

Module 3 estimates direct medical costs attributable to high BMI using a prevalence-based cost-of-illness approach adapted from Borges et al. [@Borges2025]. The module uses the Portuguese National Health Service cost matrix for 2018, including inpatient, outpatient, and pharmacological costs associated with overweight- and obesity-related diseases.

Disease-specific high-BMI population-attributable fractions (PAFs) were calculated from each simulated person's BMI and the Global Burden of Disease (GBD) 2019 relative-risk functions. For every person with BMI ≥25 kg/m², the relative risk is the GBD age- and sex-specific relative risk per 5 kg/m² raised to the number of 5 kg/m² units above 22 kg/m², with BMI capped at 50 kg/m²; everyone else has a relative risk of 1. Within each sex and 5-year age band, PAF = (mean RR − 1) / mean RR, using survey weights, and age-band PAFs are combined into national PAFs with population weights.

The published Borges et al. 2018 attributable costs are rescaled by the ratio of each year's simulated PAF to the simulated 2018 high-BMI PAF, both computed with the same method. The simulated 2018 costs therefore reproduce the published costs by construction, and later years change only with the simulated BMI distribution.

Direct treatment costs for overweight and obesity were included in full in 2018, because they were already assigned to high BMI in the source cost matrix, and in later years follow the simulated prevalence of the exposure relative to 2018. Depression-related costs were excluded from the attributable total because no BMI–depression relative-risk function was applied. Costs were reported overall and by healthcare component (inpatient, outpatient, and pharmacological treatment), and stratified by sex and educational level.

Annual cost trajectories from 2018 to 2040 were estimated by recalculating the PAFs from the simulated BMI distribution in each year. Two exposures are reported: high BMI (BMI ≥25 kg/m², as in Borges et al.) and obesity only (BMI ≥30 kg/m²). Obesity-attributable costs use the obesity PAF divided by the 2018 high-BMI PAF, so they are the share of the published high-BMI costs attributable to obesity. Total disease costs are held at their 2018 level, so projected changes reflect changes in the simulated BMI distribution rather than population growth and ageing, healthcare utilisation, treatment patterns, unit costs, or disease-specific expenditure.

### Source Study and Exposure Definition

Borges et al. estimated Portuguese direct medical costs attributable to overweight and obesity combined using INSEF 2015 prevalence estimates and a high-BMI definition of BMI ≥25 kg/m². The published prevalence estimates were:

- Overweight (BMI 25.0–29.9 kg/m²): 45.4% among men, 33.1% among women, and 38.9% overall.
- Obesity (BMI ≥30 kg/m²): 24.9% among men, 32.1% among women, and 28.7% overall.
- High BMI (BMI ≥25 kg/m²): 70.3% among men and 65.2% among women.

The present analysis retains the published 2018 cost matrix but uses simulated 2018 BMI-category prevalence in the PAF calculations. @tbl-module3-exposure-prevalence compares the published INSEF 2015 prevalence estimates with the corresponding simulated values.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-module3-exposure-prevalence
#| echo: false
#| tbl-cap: "Published INSEF 2015 prevalence estimates reported by Borges et al. [@Borges2025] and simulated 2018 BMI-category prevalence used in Module 3."

simulated_bmi_prevalence_2018 <- simulation_historical |>
  dplyr::filter(alive, year == 2018L) |>
  dplyr::group_by(simulation, sex) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    p_overweight = weighted.mean(bmi >= 25 & bmi < 30, w = survey_weight, na.rm = TRUE),
    p_obesity    = weighted.mean(bmi >= 30,             w = survey_weight, na.rm = TRUE),
    p_high_bmi   = weighted.mean(bmi >= 25,             w = survey_weight, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  dplyr::group_by(sex) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    dplyr::across(
      c(p_overweight, p_obesity, p_high_bmi),
      ~ format_interval(mean(.x), q_lo(.x), q_hi(.x), scale = 100)
    ),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    sex    = dplyr::recode(sex, men = "Males", women = "Females"),
    source = "Simulated population, 2018, mean (95% simulation interval)"
  )

dplyr::bind_rows(
  obesity_prevalence_2018() |>
    dplyr::mutate(
      dplyr::across(
        c(p_overweight, p_obesity, p_high_bmi),
        ~ format_interval(.x, NA_real_, NA_real_, scale = 100)
      ),
      source = "INSEF 2015 / Borges et al."
    ),
  simulated_bmi_prevalence_2018
) |>
  dplyr::select(source, sex, p_overweight, p_obesity, p_high_bmi) |>
  gt::gt(groupname_col = "source") |>
  gt::tab_spanner(
    label   = "BMI-category prevalence, %",
    columns = c(p_overweight, p_obesity, p_high_bmi)
  ) |>
  gt::cols_label(
    sex         = "Sex",
    p_overweight = "Overweight (25–<30)",
    p_obesity    = "Obesity (≥30)",
    p_high_bmi   = "High BMI (≥25)"
  ) |>
  gt::tab_source_note(
    gt::md("INSEF 2015 estimates from Borges et al. (2025); simulated values
           from simeq 2018 annual cycle using survey-weighted BMI distributions.")
  ) |>
  gt::opt_stylize(style = 1, color = "gray") |>
  gt::opt_table_font(font = gt::google_font("Source Sans Pro")) |>
  gt::tab_options(table.width = gt::pct(100), table.font.size = 11)
```

```{r}
  "gallbladder_biliary_diseases","Gallbladder and biliary diseases",
  "asthma",                     "Asthma",
  "cataracts",                  "Cataracts"
)

costs_2018 |>
  dplyr::left_join(disease_labels, by = "disease_group") |>
  dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(total)) |>
  dplyr::select(description, inpatient, outpatient, pharmacological, total) |>
```

### GBD Relative Risks for PAF Derivation {#sec-gbd-rr}

Disease-specific BMI relative-risk functions were obtained from the Global Burden of Disease Study 2019 relative-risk dataset [@GBD2019RR]. In the GBD comparative risk-assessment framework, high BMI is represented as a continuous exposure, with age- and sex-specific relative-risk functions for selected disease outcomes.

In this analysis, each simulated person's own BMI enters the relative-risk function, per 5 kg/m² above a reference BMI of 22 kg/m² and capped at 50 kg/m². This follows the continuous-exposure approach of the GBD framework rather than assigning one representative BMI per category.

```{r}
#| label: load-gbd-rr
#| include: false

gbd_rr_path <- file.path(
  project_root,
  "inst",
  "extdata",
  "gbd_rr_2019.xlsx"
)

if (!file.exists(gbd_rr_path)) {
  stop(
    "GBD relative-risk workbook not found at:\n",
    gbd_rr_path,
    "\nIt is bundled with the package in inst/extdata/.",
    call. = FALSE
  )
}

gbd_rr_matrix <- read_gbd_bmi_rr(path = gbd_rr_path)
```

### Cost Data Loading and Validation

Published costs are expressed in thousands of 2018 euros and reflect the Portuguese National Health Service perspective reported by Borges et al. [@Borges2025].

Published INSEF 2015 prevalence estimates and the Borges et al. PAFs are retained as comparators. PAFs are calculated from the simulated 2018 individual BMI distribution.

```{r}
#| label: load-cost-inputs
#| include: false

costs_2018 <- obesity_direct_costs_2018()
pafs_ow_ob <- obesity_overweight_pafs()
cost_mapping <- obesity_cost_outcome_mapping()
published_prevalence_2018 <- obesity_prevalence_2018()

required_cost_columns <- c(
  "disease_group",
  "inpatient",
  "outpatient",
  "pharmacological",
  "total"
)

missing_cost_columns <- setdiff(
  required_cost_columns,
  names(costs_2018)
)

if (length(missing_cost_columns) > 0L) {
  stop(
    "`obesity_direct_costs_2018()` lacks required columns: ",
    paste(missing_cost_columns, collapse = ", "),
    call. = FALSE
  )
}
```


### High-BMI Attributable Cost Scenario for 2018

High-BMI PAFs are calculated from each simulated person's 2018 BMI (@sec-gbd-rr). Because costs are rescaled to the simulated 2018 high-BMI PAF, the 2018 attributable costs equal the published Borges et al. costs for every included disease group; the simulated and published PAFs are compared as an audit.

Published direct treatment costs for overweight and obesity are included separately at 100% attribution. Depression is excluded from the attributable total because no BMI-to-depression relative-risk function is applied.

```{r}
#| label: run-module3-costs
#| cache: false

exclude_groups <- c("obesity_overweight", "depression")

direct_obesity_costs <- costs_2018 |>
  filter(disease_group == "obesity_overweight")

depression_costs <- costs_2018 |>
  filter(disease_group == "depression")

if (nrow(direct_obesity_costs) != 1L) {
  stop("Expected exactly one `obesity_overweight` cost row.", call. = FALSE)
}
if (nrow(depression_costs) != 1L) {
  stop("Expected exactly one `depression` cost row.", call. = FALSE)
}

# ── Step 1: simulated 2018 prevalence by sex ────────────────────────────────
prevalence_2018_sim <- simulation_historical |>
  filter(alive, year == 2018L) |>
  group_by(sex) |>
  summarise(
    p_overweight = weighted.mean(bmi >= 25 & bmi < 30, w = survey_weight, na.rm = TRUE),
    p_obesity    = weighted.mean(bmi >= 30,             w = survey_weight, na.rm = TRUE),
    p_high_bmi   = weighted.mean(bmi >= 25,             w = survey_weight, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(sex = dplyr::recode(sex, men = "Males", women = "Females"))

# ── Step 2: high-BMI PAFs from individual 2018 BMI ─────────────────────────
# Each person's BMI enters the GBD RR per 5 kg/m² above 22 (capped at 50);
# PAF = (mean RR - 1) / mean RR within sex x 5-year age band.
pafs_high_bmi <- calculate_obesity_pafs_individual(
  simulation_output = simulation_historical,
  year              = 2018L,
  rr_matrix         = gbd_rr_matrix
)

# ── Step 3: 2018 attributable costs ─────────────────────────────────────────
# Costs are rescaled to the simulated 2018 high-BMI PAF, so 2018 reproduces
# the published Borges et al. costs for every included group (depression is
# excluded). The 2018 row of the annual cost calculation is used directly.
costs_2018_attributable <- calculate_annual_obesity_costs(
  simulation_output      = simulation_historical,
  gbd_rr_matrix          = gbd_rr_matrix,
  costs_dro              = costs_2018,
  outcome_mapping        = cost_mapping,
  exclude_disease_groups = exclude_groups,
  years                  = 2018L,
  exposure               = "high_bmi",
  weight_col             = "survey_weight"
)$by_year_disease |>
  dplyr::filter(year == 2018L)

costs_by_group_2018 <- costs_2018_attributable |>
  dplyr::filter(!disease_group %in% exclude_groups)

# PAF audit: simulated 2018 high-BMI PAF by cost group against the PAF
# implicit in the Borges et al. matrix (published comparator only).
paf_audit_2018 <- costs_by_group_2018 |>
  dplyr::select(disease_group, paf_simulated_2018 = paf_obesity) |>
  dplyr::left_join(
    pafs_ow_ob |>
      dplyr::transmute(disease_group, paf_borges_published = paf_ow_ob),
    by = "disease_group"
  )

# 95% simulation interval for the simulated 2018 PAF: the same calculation
# run on each replication's 2018 records.
simulation_2018 <- simulation_historical |>
  dplyr::filter(year == 2018L)

paf_2018_by_simulation <- lapply(
  split(simulation_2018, simulation_2018$simulation),
  function(sim_data) {
    calculate_annual_obesity_costs(
      simulation_output      = sim_data,
      gbd_rr_matrix          = gbd_rr_matrix,
      costs_dro              = costs_2018,
      outcome_mapping        = cost_mapping,
      exclude_disease_groups = exclude_groups,
      years                  = 2018L,
      exposure               = "high_bmi",
      weight_col             = "survey_weight"
    )$by_year_disease |>
      dplyr::filter(year == 2018L, !disease_group %in% exclude_groups) |>
      dplyr::select(disease_group, paf_obesity)
  }
) |>
  dplyr::bind_rows(.id = "simulation")

paf_audit_2018 <- paf_audit_2018 |>
  dplyr::left_join(
    paf_2018_by_simulation |>
      dplyr::summarise(
        paf_simulated_2018_lo = q_lo(paf_obesity),
        paf_simulated_2018_hi = q_hi(paf_obesity),
        .by = disease_group
      ),
    by = "disease_group"
  )
rm(simulation_2018)

write_result_csv(prevalence_2018_sim,            "module3_simulated_bmi_prevalence_2018.csv")
write_result_csv(pafs_high_bmi$paf_by_outcome,   "module3_high_bmi_pafs_by_outcome_2018.csv")
write_result_csv(paf_audit_2018,                 "module3_high_bmi_paf_audit_2018.csv")
write_result_csv(costs_by_group_2018,            "module3_high_bmi_costs_by_group_2018.csv")
```

```{r}
#| label: create-module3-combined-total
#| include: false

required_published_cost_columns <- c(
  "inpatient",

cost_components <- bind_rows(

)



combined_obesity_cost_total <- bind_rows(
  cost_components,

      component = "Combined high-BMI-attributable costs",

) |>
  select(

    total_k_eur
  )

write_result_csv(
  combined_obesity_cost_total,
  "module3_combined_obesity_cost_total_2018.csv"
)
```

### Interpretation and Limitations

Module 3 estimates direct medical costs attributable to high BMI, using a prevalence-based cost-of-illness approach adapted from Borges et al. [@Borges2025]. The analysis adopts the Portuguese 2018 National Health Service cost matrix, including inpatient, outpatient, and pharmacological costs for overweight- and obesity-related diseases.

The scenario has not been independently validated against another Portuguese cost year, administrative-cost source, or patient-level healthcare-use dataset. Total disease costs are held at their 2018 level, so projections do not reflect population growth, ageing, or changes in healthcare use. Age-band PAFs are combined into national PAFs with population weights rather than cost weights, because the published costs are not available by age.

### Annual Cost Trajectories, 2018–2040 {#sec-cost-trajectories}

**Starting point: Borges et al. 2018 costs anchored to INSEF 2015 prevalence.** The published cost matrix reports direct medical costs already attributable to high BMI — that is, each disease-specific entry is the total disease cost multiplied by a PAF derived from INSEF 2015 high-BMI prevalence estimates (overweight 38.9 %; obesity 28.7 %; high BMI ≥ 25 kg/m²: 70.3 % in men, 65.2 % in women). These 2018-euro figures serve as the cost anchor.

**Annual PAF rescaling.** For each year $t$ in 2018–2040, the model recomputes PAFs from each simulated person's BMI (@sec-gbd-rr) and rescales the published cost matrix:

$$
C_{d,t} = C_{d,\text{Borges}} \times \frac{PAF_{d,t}^{\text{sim}}}{PAF_{d,2018}^{\text{sim, high BMI}}}
$$

where $C_{d,\text{Borges}}$ is the Borges et al. attributable cost, $PAF_{d,t}^{\text{sim}}$ is the simulated PAF for disease $d$ in year $t$, and $PAF_{d,2018}^{\text{sim, high BMI}}$ is the simulated high-BMI PAF in 2018. Both PAFs use the same method, so 2018 reproduces the published costs and later years change only with the simulated BMI distribution. For high-BMI costs, $PAF_{d,t}^{\text{sim}}$ counts everyone with BMI ≥25 kg/m²; for obesity-only costs it counts only BMI ≥30 kg/m², giving the share of the published high-BMI costs attributable to obesity. Direct treatment costs for overweight and obesity follow the simulated prevalence of the exposure relative to 2018. Unit healthcare costs are held constant in real terms (`unit_cost_annual_growth = 0`): trajectory changes reflect shifts in BMI-category prevalence and population composition only, not changes in treatment patterns or healthcare utilisation rates.

```{r}
#| label: set-discount-rate

# Annual discount rate for the 2026 present-value series. Defined here so the
# methods text, table notes and cost runs below all use the same value.
discount_rate <- 0.04
discount_rate_pct <- paste0(format(100 * discount_rate, trim = TRUE), "%")
```

**Monetary adjustment and discounting.** All annual costs are first expressed in constant 2018 euros (`total_keur_2018_constant`). Two nominal series are then derived using Portuguese HICP annual average indices sourced from Eurostat (dataset PRC_HICP_AIND, all-items CP00, rescaled to 2018 = 100; 2026 is estimated from current rates as of September 2026 at approximately 3.0 % per year):

- `total_keur_year_nominal`: each year's cost multiplied by that year's HICP index, giving the cost expressed in the price level of that actual calendar year — the appropriate series for a year-by-year budget impact analysis.
- `total_keur_2026_nominal`: every year's cost converted to the common 2026 price level (HICP index 124.35 relative to 2018 = 100), used as input to the present-value calculation.

Projected costs beyond 2026 are discounted to 2026 present value at `r discount_rate_pct` per year (`discount_rate` = `r discount_rate`). The `total_keur_2018_constant` series remains the recommended primary output for international comparisons and sensitivity analyses.

```{r}
#| label: run-cost-trajectory
#| cache: false

# ── Portuguese HICP, 2018 = 100 ─────────────────────────────────────────────
# Source: Eurostat PRC_HICP_AIND, all-items (CP00), annual average index
# (2015 = 100), rescaled so that 2018 = 100. Retrieved 2026-09-10.
# 2026 is estimated from Eurostat annual rates as of Aug 2026 (~3.0 % p.a.).
# Update data-raw/cpi_portugal_hicp_2018base.csv annually from Eurostat;
# no changes to this script are needed.
cpi_portugal <- read.csv(
  file.path(data_raw_dir, "cpi_portugal_hicp_2018base.csv")
)

# Derive the scalar from the table so there is a single source of truth
cpi_2026 <- cpi_portugal$cpi_index[cpi_portugal$year == 2026L]
# discount_rate is set in the set-discount-rate chunk above.

# Costs are computed for 2000-2040. Years before the 2018 cost anchor are
# back-cast: the 2018 cost structure is applied to that year's simulated BMI
# distribution. Only the outcome tables (reported_years) use the back-cast
# years; the budget, nominal and present-value tables start in 2018.
# The two cost runs take several minutes with 50 replications, so their
# results are cached next to the simulation file. Delete this file if the
# cost inputs, CPI table or GBD relative risks change.
cost_cache_file <- file.path(
  results_dir,
  paste0(
    "module3_annual_costs_2000_2040_", simulation_version,
    "_nsim", n_simulations_main, ".rds"
  )
)

if (file.exists(cost_cache_file)) {
  cost_cache <- readRDS(cost_cache_file)
  annual_costs <- cost_cache$high_bmi
  annual_costs_obesity <- cost_cache$obesity
} else {
  annual_costs <- calculate_annual_obesity_costs(
    simulation_output = simulation_historical,
    gbd_rr_matrix = gbd_rr_matrix,
    costs_dro = costs_2018,
    outcome_mapping = cost_mapping,
    exclude_disease_groups = c(
      "obesity_overweight",
      "depression"
    ),
    years = 2000L:2040L,
    exposure = "high_bmi",
    bmi_reference = 22,
    weight_col = "survey_weight",
    base_cost_year = 2018L,
    unit_cost_annual_growth = 0,
    cpi_2026 = cpi_2026,
    cpi_table = cpi_portugal,
    discount_rate = discount_rate,
    discount_base_year = 2026L,
    by_simulation = TRUE
  )

  # Same method, obesity only (BMI >= 30): the share of the published
  # high-BMI costs attributable to obesity.
  annual_costs_obesity <- calculate_annual_obesity_costs(
    simulation_output = simulation_historical,
    gbd_rr_matrix = gbd_rr_matrix,
    costs_dro = costs_2018,
    outcome_mapping = cost_mapping,
    exclude_disease_groups = c(
      "obesity_overweight",
      "depression"
    ),
    years = 2000L:2040L,
    exposure = "obesity",
    bmi_reference = 22,
    weight_col = "survey_weight",
    base_cost_year = 2018L,
    unit_cost_annual_growth = 0,
    cpi_2026 = cpi_2026,
    cpi_table = cpi_portugal,
    discount_rate = discount_rate,
    discount_base_year = 2026L,
    by_simulation = TRUE
  )

  saveRDS(
    list(high_bmi = annual_costs, obesity = annual_costs_obesity),
    cost_cache_file
  )
}

if (!all(c("totals", "by_year_disease") %in% names(annual_costs))) {
  stop(
    "`calculate_annual_obesity_costs()` must return both ",
    "`totals` and `by_year_disease`.",
    call. = FALSE
  )
}

# Keep the full 2000-2040 replication totals for the outcome tables, then
# restrict every cost table to 2018 onwards.
cost_totals_by_sim_all <- annual_costs$totals_by_simulation
cost_totals_by_sim_all_obesity <- annual_costs_obesity$totals_by_simulation
from_2018 <- function(res) lapply(res, function(d) if (is.data.frame(d) && "year" %in% names(d)) d[as.integer(d$year) >= 2018L, , drop = FALSE] else d)
annual_costs <- from_2018(annual_costs)
annual_costs_obesity <- from_2018(annual_costs_obesity)

cost_trajectory    <- annual_costs$totals
cost_trajectory_obesity <- annual_costs_obesity$totals
cost_by_disease_yr <- annual_costs$by_year_disease
cost_by_sex        <- annual_costs$by_sex_totals
cost_by_sex_disease <- annual_costs$by_sex_disease

required_cost_trajectory_columns <- c(
  "year",
  "total_keur_2018_constant",
  "total_keur_2026_nominal",
  "discount_factor",
  "total_keur_2026_pv"
)

missing_cost_trajectory_columns <- setdiff(
  required_cost_trajectory_columns,
  names(cost_trajectory)
)

if (length(missing_cost_trajectory_columns) > 0L) {
  stop(
    "`annual_costs$totals` is missing: ",
    paste(missing_cost_trajectory_columns, collapse = ", "),
    "\n\nAvailable columns:\n",
    paste(names(cost_trajectory), collapse = ", "),
    call. = FALSE
  )
}

sim_prev_detail <- simulation_historical |>
  dplyr::filter(
    alive,
    year >= 2018L,
    year <= 2040L
  ) |>
  dplyr::group_by(
    year,
    sex,
    education_level
  ) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    high_bmi_prev = weighted.mean(
      bmi >= 25,
      w = survey_weight,
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),
    overweight_prev = weighted.mean(
      bmi >= 25 & bmi < 30,
      w = survey_weight,
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),
    obesity_prev = weighted.mean(
      bmi >= 30,
      w = survey_weight,
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),
    population_weight = sum(
      survey_weight,
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

sim_prev_combined <- sim_prev_detail |>
  dplyr::group_by(year) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    high_bmi_prev = weighted.mean(
      high_bmi_prev,
      w = population_weight,
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

write_result_csv(
  cost_trajectory,
  "module3_cost_trajectory_2018_2040.csv"
)

write_result_csv(
  cost_trajectory_obesity,
  "module3_cost_trajectory_obesity_2018_2040.csv"
)

write_result_csv(
  cost_by_disease_yr,
  "module3_cost_by_disease_year.csv"
)

write_result_csv(

)

write_result_csv(
  sim_prev_combined,
  "module3_high_bmi_prevalence_combined_2018_2040.csv"
)
```

### Sensitivity to the GBD relative risks {#sec-cost-rr-sensitivity}

The simulation intervals above reflect Monte Carlo variation only. To show how much the cost estimates depend on the GBD 2019 relative risks, the cost calculation is repeated with every relative risk set to the lower bound of its 95% uncertainty interval, and then to the upper bound. All outcomes, sexes and age bands move to the same bound together, so the range brackets the effect of relative-risk uncertainty rather than giving a probabilistic interval. These runs use all replications pooled.

Because each run anchors to its own simulated 2018 high-BMI PAF, the 2018 high-BMI cost equals the Borges et al. figure under every bound. The relative risks therefore change how fast costs move after 2018 and the share of costs attributable to obesity, not the starting level.

```{r}
#| label: run-cost-rr-sensitivity

rr_sensitivity_cache_file <- file.path(
  results_dir,
  paste0(
    "module3_rr_sensitivity_", simulation_version,
    "_nsim", n_simulations_main, ".rds"
  )
)

if (file.exists(rr_sensitivity_cache_file)) {
  cost_rr_sensitivity <- readRDS(rr_sensitivity_cache_file)
} else {
  rr_sensitivity_grid <- tidyr::expand_grid(
    rr_bound = c("lower", "point", "upper"),
    exposure = c("high_bmi", "obesity")
  )

  cost_rr_sensitivity <- purrr::pmap(
    rr_sensitivity_grid,
    function(rr_bound, exposure) {
      calculate_annual_obesity_costs(
        simulation_output = simulation_historical,
        gbd_rr_matrix = select_gbd_rr_bound(gbd_rr_matrix, rr_bound),
        costs_dro = costs_2018,
        outcome_mapping = cost_mapping,
        exclude_disease_groups = c("obesity_overweight", "depression"),
        years = 2018L:2040L,
        exposure = exposure,
        bmi_reference = 22,
        weight_col = "survey_weight",
        base_cost_year = 2018L,
        unit_cost_annual_growth = 0,
        cpi_2026 = cpi_2026,
        cpi_table = cpi_portugal,
        discount_rate = discount_rate,
        discount_base_year = 2026L,
        by_simulation = FALSE
      )$totals |>
        dplyr::select(year, total_keur_2018_constant, total_keur_2026_pv) |>
        dplyr::mutate(rr_bound = rr_bound, exposure = exposure, .before = 1L)
    }
  ) |>
    dplyr::bind_rows()

  saveRDS(cost_rr_sensitivity, rr_sensitivity_cache_file)
}

write_result_csv(
  cost_rr_sensitivity,
  "module3_cost_rr_sensitivity_2018_2040.csv"
)
```

Thousands of constant 2018 euros; all replications pooled. The final row sums 2018–2040 in 2026 present value (", discount_rate_pct, " per year).")

### High-BMI Cost Trajectories Stratified by Sex and Education, 2018–2040

GBD 2019 does not provide education-specific relative-risk functions for BMI-attributable diseases, so disease-specific PAFs cannot be computed separately by educational level. Instead, the combined annual cost total is allocated across sex × education strata in proportion to each group's simulated **disease-burden share** — the product of high-BMI prevalence and survey-weighted population size.

For each year, the burden share of group $g$ is:

$$\text{share}_{g,t} = \frac{p_{g,t} \times N_{g,t}}{\sum_g p_{g,t} \times N_{g,t}}$$

and the group-specific annual cost is $C_{g,t} = C_t \times \text{share}_{g,t}$, where $C_t$ is the overall prevalence-scaled cost trajectory from @sec-cost-trajectories. By construction, group costs sum to the total in every year. This is a prevalence-proportional approximation: no education-specific relative risks are applied because GBD 2019 does not provide them. Because lower-SES groups may carry higher relative risks at a given BMI [@Stringhini2017], it probably understates the cost share of the low-education group.

```{r}
#| label: run-stratified-cost-trajectory
#| cache: false

cost_trajectory_by_group <- sim_prev_detail |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    burden = high_bmi_prev * population_weight
  ) |>
  dplyr::group_by(year) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    total_burden = sum(burden, na.rm = TRUE),
    burden_share = dplyr::if_else(
      total_burden > 0,
      burden / total_burden,
      NA_real_
    )
  ) |>
  dplyr::ungroup() |>
  dplyr::left_join(
    cost_trajectory |>
      dplyr::select(
        year,
        total_keur_2018_constant,
        total_keur_2026_nominal,
        total_keur_2026_pv
      ),
    by = "year"
  ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    cost_constant_2018eur =
      total_keur_2018_constant * burden_share,
    cost_2026eur_nominal =
      total_keur_2026_nominal * burden_share,
    cost_2026pv =
      total_keur_2026_pv * burden_share,
    education_level = factor(
      education_level,
      levels = c("low", "medium", "high")
    )
  ) |>
  dplyr::select(
    year,
    sex,
    education_level,
    high_bmi_prev,
    population_weight,
    burden_share,
    cost_constant_2018eur,
    cost_2026eur_nominal,
    cost_2026pv
  )

write_result_csv(
  cost_trajectory_by_group,
  "module3_high_bmi_cost_trajectory_by_sex_education.csv"
)

# ── Two-group education collapse ─────────────────────────────────────────────
# Lower education: low + medium (up to secondary)
# Higher education: high (tertiary)
cost_trajectory_by_2group <- cost_trajectory_by_group |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    education_2group = factor(
      dplyr::case_when(
        as.character(education_level) %in% c("low", "medium") ~ "Lower education",
        as.character(education_level) == "high"               ~ "Higher education"
      ),
      levels = c("Lower education", "Higher education")
    )
  ) |>
  dplyr::group_by(year, sex, education_2group) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    # Prevalence: population-weighted mean across subgroups
    high_bmi_prev         = weighted.mean(high_bmi_prev, w = population_weight, na.rm = TRUE),
    population_weight     = sum(population_weight,     na.rm = TRUE),
    # Costs and burden shares: additive
    burden_share          = sum(burden_share,          na.rm = TRUE),
    cost_constant_2018eur = sum(cost_constant_2018eur, na.rm = TRUE),
    cost_2026eur_nominal  = sum(cost_2026eur_nominal,  na.rm = TRUE),
    cost_2026pv           = sum(cost_2026pv,           na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    sex = factor(sex, levels = c("women", "men"))
  )

write_result_csv(
  cost_trajectory_by_2group,
  "module3_high_bmi_cost_trajectory_by_sex_education2group.csv"
)
```





```{r}
#| label: stratified-cost-intervals
#| include: false

# 95% simulation intervals for the stratified tables: prevalence, burden
# share and allocated cost computed within each replication, using that
# replication's national cost total.
strat_by_simulation <- simulation_historical |>
  dplyr::filter(alive, year %in% c(2018L, 2040L)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    education_2group = dplyr::if_else(
      education_level == "high", "Higher education", "Lower education"
    )
  ) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    high_bmi_prev     = weighted.mean(bmi >= 25, w = survey_weight, na.rm = TRUE),
    population_weight = sum(survey_weight, na.rm = TRUE),
    .by = c(simulation, year, sex, education_level, education_2group)
  ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(burden = high_bmi_prev * population_weight) |>
  dplyr::mutate(burden_share = burden / sum(burden), .by = c(simulation, year)) |>
  dplyr::left_join(
    annual_costs$totals_by_simulation |>
      dplyr::select(simulation, year, total_keur_2018_constant),
    by = c("simulation", "year")
  ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(cost_constant_2018eur = total_keur_2018_constant * burden_share)

summarise_strat_intervals <- function(data) {
  data |>
    dplyr::summarise(
      dplyr::across(
        c(high_bmi_prev, burden_share, cost_constant_2018eur),
        list(lo = q_lo, hi = q_hi)
      ),
      .by = c(year, sex, group)
    )
}

strat_intervals_3group <- strat_by_simulation |>
  dplyr::rename(group = education_level) |>
  summarise_strat_intervals()

strat_intervals_2group <- strat_by_simulation |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    high_bmi_prev = weighted.mean(high_bmi_prev, w = population_weight),
    burden_share = sum(burden_share),
    cost_constant_2018eur = sum(cost_constant_2018eur),
    .by = c(simulation, year, sex, education_2group)
  ) |>
  dplyr::rename(group = education_2group) |>
  summarise_strat_intervals()
```

```{r}
#| label: burden-share-text-values
#| include: false

low_edu_values <- cost_trajectory_by_group |>
  dplyr::filter(year %in% c(2018L, 2040L), education_level == "low") |>
  dplyr::select(year, sex, high_bmi_prev, burden_share, population_weight)

low_edu_value <- function(sx, yr, col) {
  low_edu_values[[col]][low_edu_values$sex == sx & low_edu_values$year == yr]
}
pct_text <- function(x) sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * x)
low_edu_shrink <- function(sx) {
  1 - low_edu_value(sx, 2040L, "population_weight") /
    low_edu_value(sx, 2018L, "population_weight")
}
```

The burden shares require careful interpretation. The low-education group shows a **declining share** in both sexes (women: `r pct_text(low_edu_value("women", 2018L, "burden_share"))` in 2018 to `r pct_text(low_edu_value("women", 2040L, "burden_share"))` in 2040; men: `r pct_text(low_edu_value("men", 2018L, "burden_share"))` to `r pct_text(low_edu_value("men", 2040L, "burden_share"))`), while medium- and high-education shares rise. This pattern does not reflect a narrowing of socioeconomic inequalities in high-BMI prevalence. Simulated high-BMI prevalence rises in all groups (low-education women: `r pct_text(low_edu_value("women", 2018L, "high_bmi_prev"))` to `r pct_text(low_edu_value("women", 2040L, "high_bmi_prev"))`; low-education men: `r pct_text(low_edu_value("men", 2018L, "high_bmi_prev"))` to `r pct_text(low_edu_value("men", 2040L, "high_bmi_prev"))`). The declining burden share is instead driven by a demographic shift: the simulated low-education population shrinks by `r pct_text(low_edu_shrink("women"))` among women and `r pct_text(low_edu_shrink("men"))` among men between 2018 and 2040, reflecting Portugal's ongoing rise in educational attainment. As fewer individuals are classified as low-education, their aggregate contribution to total population-level burden decreases even though per-person risk remains elevated.

### Attributable Costs by BMI Class, 2018 {#sec-cost-bmi-class}

This section splits the 2018 high-BMI-attributable costs across four mutually exclusive BMI classes: overweight (25.0–29.9 kg/m²), obesity class I (30.0–34.9 kg/m²), obesity class II (35.0–39.9 kg/m²), and obesity class III (≥40 kg/m²). It uses the same individual-level relative risks as the PAF calculation (@sec-gbd-rr). For each GBD outcome and each simulated person $i$ with BMI ≥25 kg/m², the excess risk is

$$RR_i - 1 = rr_{5}^{\,(\min(\text{BMI}_i,\,50) - 22)/5} - 1,$$

where $rr_5$ is the GBD relative risk per 5 kg/m² for that person's sex and 5-year age band. The excess risk, multiplied by the survey weight, is summed within each BMI class $c$, and the class share for the outcome is

$$\text{share}_c = \frac{\sum_{i \in c} w_i\,(RR_i - 1)}{\sum_{i:\,\text{BMI}_i \ge 25} w_i\,(RR_i - 1)}.$$

Outcome shares are averaged within each cost group, in the same way the outcome PAFs are combined into the group PAF, and each group's 2018 attributable cost is multiplied by its class shares. The direct overweight-and-obesity treatment costs have no relative risk and are split by the prevalence of each class among people with BMI ≥25 kg/m². The split is computed within each simulation replication; the tables show the mean across replications and, for the totals, the 95% simulation interval.

```{r}
#| label: run-bmi-class-costs
#| cache: false

bmi_class_levels <- c("overweight", "obesity_I", "obesity_II", "obesity_III")

# ── Step 1: 2018 high-BMI population with class and excess BMI units ────────
# Rows are selected before converting, so the full simulation output is
# not copied (it can take several GB with 50 replications).
class_people_2018 <- data.table::as.data.table(
  simulation_historical[
    which(
      simulation_historical$year == 2018L & simulation_historical$alive &
        simulation_historical$age >= 20L & simulation_historical$age <= 84L &
        simulation_historical$bmi >= 25 &
        simulation_historical$survey_weight > 0
    ),
    c("simulation", "sex", "age", "bmi", "survey_weight")
  ]
)[, .(
  simulation,
  sex = dplyr::recode(as.character(sex), men = "Males", women = "Females"),
  age_band = paste0(((age - 20L) %/% 5L) * 5L + 20L, "-",
                    ((age - 20L) %/% 5L) * 5L + 24L),
  bmi_class = data.table::fcase(
    bmi < 30, "overweight",
    bmi < 35, "obesity_I",
    bmi < 40, "obesity_II",
    default = "obesity_III"
  ),
  weight = survey_weight,
  excess_units = (pmin(bmi, 50) - 22) / 5
)]

# BMI-class prevalence among people with BMI >= 25 (direct treatment split)
class_prevalence_2018 <- class_people_2018[
  , .(class_weight = sum(weight)), by = .(simulation, bmi_class)
][, class_share := class_weight / sum(class_weight), by = simulation]

# ── Step 2: GBD relative risks, mapped to cost groups ───────────────────────
gbd_to_group <- cost_mapping |>
  dplyr::transmute(
    outcome_lc = tolower(as.character(outcome_pattern)),
    disease_group
  )

class_rr <- gbd_rr_matrix |>
  dplyr::transmute(
    outcome_lc = tolower(as.character(disease)),
    sex = dplyr::recode(
      as.character(sex),
      men   = "Males",   Male   = "Males",   male   = "Males",
      women = "Females", Female = "Females", female = "Females"
    ),
    age_band = as.character(age_band),
    rr_per_5 = as.numeric(rr_per_5)
  ) |>
  dplyr::inner_join(gbd_to_group, by = "outcome_lc") |>
  dplyr::filter(disease_group %in% costs_by_group_2018$disease_group) |>
  data.table::as.data.table()

# ── Step 3: excess risk by outcome and BMI class, then class shares ─────────
class_excess <- data.table::rbindlist(lapply(
  split(class_rr, by = "outcome_lc"),
  function(rr_outcome) {
    rr_outcome[class_people_2018, on = .(sex, age_band), nomatch = 0L][
      , .(excess = sum(weight * (rr_per_5^excess_units - 1))),
      by = .(simulation, disease_group, outcome_lc, bmi_class)
    ]
  }
))

class_shares_by_group <- class_excess[
  , excess := pmax(excess, 0)
][
  , outcome_total := sum(excess), by = .(simulation, outcome_lc)
][
  outcome_total > 0
][
  , .(share = mean(excess / outcome_total)),
  by = .(simulation, disease_group, bmi_class)
] |>
  tibble::as_tibble() |>
  # Outcomes where a class has no one contribute a share of zero
  tidyr::complete(
    tidyr::nesting(simulation, disease_group),
    bmi_class = bmi_class_levels,
    fill = list(share = 0)
  ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(share = share / sum(share), .by = c(simulation, disease_group))

# A cost group with no excess risk in 2018 falls back to the prevalence split,
# so every group's cost is kept.
groups_without_excess <- setdiff(
  costs_by_group_2018$disease_group,
  class_shares_by_group$disease_group
)
if (length(groups_without_excess) > 0L) {
  class_shares_by_group <- dplyr::bind_rows(
    class_shares_by_group,
    tidyr::expand_grid(
      tibble::as_tibble(class_prevalence_2018) |>
        dplyr::select(simulation, bmi_class, share = class_share),
      disease_group = groups_without_excess
    )
  )
}

# ── Step 4: apply shares to 2018 attributable costs ─────────────────────────
costs_bmi_class_by_simulation <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  class_shares_by_group |>
    dplyr::left_join(
      costs_by_group_2018 |> dplyr::select(disease_group, total_obesity),
      by = "disease_group"
    ),
  tibble::as_tibble(class_prevalence_2018) |>
    dplyr::transmute(
      simulation,
      disease_group = "obesity_overweight",
      bmi_class,
      share = class_share,
      total_obesity = direct_obesity_costs$total
    )
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(cost = total_obesity * share)

costs_bmi_class_all <- costs_bmi_class_by_simulation |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    cost = mean(cost),
    total_obesity = mean(total_obesity),
    .by = c(disease_group, bmi_class)
  ) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(
    names_from = bmi_class, values_from = cost, values_fill = 0
  )

cost_totals_by_class <- costs_bmi_class_by_simulation |>
  dplyr::summarise(cost = sum(cost), .by = c(simulation, bmi_class)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(share = cost / sum(cost), .by = simulation) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    cost_mean  = mean(cost),  cost_lo  = q_lo(cost),  cost_hi  = q_hi(cost),
    share_mean = mean(share), share_lo = q_lo(share), share_hi = q_hi(share),
    .by = bmi_class
  ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(bmi_class = factor(bmi_class, levels = bmi_class_levels)) |>
  dplyr::arrange(bmi_class)

write_result_csv(costs_bmi_class_all, "module3_costs_by_bmi_class_2018.csv")
write_result_csv(cost_totals_by_class, "module3_cost_totals_by_bmi_class_2018.csv")
rm(class_people_2018, class_excess)
```

## Headline Outcomes, 2000–2040 {#sec-headline}

@tbl-main-selected-outcomes brings together the main outputs of the three modules, by sex and education level, with sex totals and the whole adult population. The simulation runs in annual cycles from 1998 to 2040; outcomes are reported for 2000, 2020 and 2040 only. Costs before 2018 are back-cast by applying the 2018 cost structure to that year's simulated BMI distribution.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-main-selected-outcomes
#| echo: false
#| tbl-cap: "Headline simeq outcomes from the Portuguese reference application, 2000–2040, by sex and education level. Mean across simulation replications (95% simulation interval)."

# Every outcome is computed within each simulation replication first, then
# summarised as the mean and 95% simulation interval across replications.
# Numerators and denominators are kept per sex x education stratum, so the
# sex totals and the all-adults row are exact aggregates of the strata.

selected_years <- reported_years
headline_strata <- c("simulation", "year", "sex", "education_level")

as_stratum_keys <- function(data) {
  dplyr::mutate(
    data,
    dplyr::across(c(sex, education_level), as.character),
    year = as.integer(year)
  )
}

sum_or_na <- function(x) if (all(is.na(x))) NA_real_ else sum(x, na.rm = TRUE)

module1_components <- bmi_by_rep |>
  dplyr::filter(year %in% selected_years) |>
  as_stratum_keys() |>
  dplyr::transmute(
    simulation, year, sex, education_level,
    bmi_sum    = mean_bmi * weighted_population,
    obese_n    = obesity_prevalence * weighted_population,
    high_bmi_n = (overweight_prevalence + obesity_prevalence) * weighted_population,
    population = weighted_population
  )

qaly_components <- qaly_results$individual |>
  dplyr::filter(year %in% selected_years) |>
  as_stratum_keys() |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    qaly_loss = sum(
      qaly_loss_weighted[bmi_category %in% obesity_categories],
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),
    person_years = sum(survey_weight * person_years, na.rm = TRUE),
    .by = dplyr::all_of(headline_strata)
  )

yll_components <- burden_results$by_year_sim |>
  dplyr::filter(year %in% selected_years) |>
  as_stratum_keys() |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    yll            = sum(yll_obesity_attrib_weighted, na.rm = TRUE),
    yll_population = sum(N_weighted, na.rm = TRUE),
    .by = dplyr::all_of(headline_strata)
  )

# National costs per replication, allocated to sex x education strata in
# proportion to each stratum's share of the exposed population (BMI >= 25
# for high-BMI costs, BMI >= 30 for obesity costs), as in the stratified
# cost tables above. GBD has no education-specific relative risks.
national_costs_by_sim <- dplyr::full_join(
  cost_totals_by_sim_all |>
    dplyr::transmute(simulation, year = as.integer(year),
                     cost_high_bmi_total = total_keur_2018_constant / 1000),
  cost_totals_by_sim_all_obesity |>
    dplyr::transmute(simulation, year = as.integer(year),
                     cost_obesity_total = total_keur_2018_constant / 1000),
  by = c("simulation", "year")
)

headline_components <- module1_components |>
  dplyr::left_join(qaly_components, by = headline_strata) |>
  dplyr::left_join(yll_components, by = headline_strata) |>
  dplyr::left_join(national_costs_by_sim, by = c("simulation", "year")) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    cost_high_bmi = cost_high_bmi_total * high_bmi_n / sum(high_bmi_n),
    cost_obesity  = cost_obesity_total * obese_n / sum(obese_n),
    .by = c(simulation, year)
  ) |>
  dplyr::select(-cost_high_bmi_total, -cost_obesity_total)

additive_columns <- c(
  "bmi_sum", "obese_n", "high_bmi_n", "population", "qaly_loss",
  "person_years", "yll", "yll_population", "cost_high_bmi", "cost_obesity"
)

headline_by_sim <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  headline_components,
  headline_components |>
    dplyr::summarise(
      dplyr::across(dplyr::all_of(additive_columns), sum_or_na),
      .by = c(simulation, year, sex)
    ) |>
    dplyr::mutate(education_level = "all"),
  headline_components |>
    dplyr::summarise(
      dplyr::across(dplyr::all_of(additive_columns), sum_or_na),
      .by = c(simulation, year)
    ) |>
    dplyr::mutate(sex = "all", education_level = "all")
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    mean_bmi           = bmi_sum / population,
    obesity_prevalence = obese_n / population,
    qaly_loss_per100k  = 1e5 * qaly_loss / person_years,
    yll_per_100k       = 1e5 * yll / yll_population
  )

headline_outcomes <- tibble::tribble(
  ~Modules, ~outcome,                                                                        ~variable,            ~scale, ~digits,
  "I",      "Mean BMI, kg/m²",                                                               "mean_bmi",           1,      2,
  "I",      "Obesity prevalence, %",                                                         "obesity_prevalence", 100,    1,
  "II",     "Obesity-attributable QALY loss per 100,000 adults",                             "qaly_loss_per100k",  1,      0,
  "II",     "Obesity-attributable YLL per 100,000 adults",                                   "yll_per_100k",       1,      0,
  "III",    "High-BMI-attributable direct medical costs, € million (constant 2018 prices)",  "cost_high_bmi",      1,      1,
  "III",    "Obesity-attributable direct medical costs, € million (constant 2018 prices)",   "cost_obesity",       1,      1
)

table_2_numeric <- purrr::pmap_dfr(
  headline_outcomes,
  function(Modules, outcome, variable, scale, digits) {
    headline_by_sim |>
      dplyr::filter(is.finite(.data[[variable]])) |>
      dplyr::summarise(
        mean  = mean(.data[[variable]]),
        lower = q_lo(.data[[variable]]),
        upper = q_hi(.data[[variable]]),
        .by = c(year, sex, education_level)
      ) |>
      dplyr::mutate(
        Modules = Modules, outcome = outcome,
        value = format_interval(mean, lower, upper, digits = digits, scale = scale),
        .before = 1L
      )
  }
)

write_result_csv(table_2_numeric, "table_2_selected_outcomes_intervals.csv")

population_levels <- c(
  "Women, low education", "Women, medium education", "Women, high education", "Women, all",
  "Men, low education", "Men, medium education", "Men, high education", "Men, all",
  "All adults"
)

population_label <- function(sex, education_level) {
  sex_label <- dplyr::recode(sex, women = "Women", men = "Men")
  dplyr::case_when(
    sex == "all"             ~ "All adults",
    education_level == "all" ~ paste0(sex_label, ", all"),
    TRUE                     ~ paste0(sex_label, ", ", education_level, " education")
  )
}

# Costs before 2018 are back-cast with the 2018 cost structure.
table_2_long <- tidyr::expand_grid(
  dplyr::distinct(table_2_numeric, Modules, outcome, sex, education_level),
  year = selected_years
) |>
  dplyr::left_join(
    table_2_numeric |>
      dplyr::select(Modules, outcome, sex, education_level, year, value),
    by = c("Modules", "outcome", "sex", "education_level", "year")
  ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    value = dplyr::coalesce(value, "—"),
    Population = factor(population_label(sex, education_level), levels = population_levels)
  ) |>
  dplyr::select(-sex, -education_level)

table_2 <- table_2_long |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(
    names_from = year,
    values_from = value
  ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    Modules = factor(Modules, levels = c("I", "II", "III")),
    outcome = factor(outcome, levels = headline_outcomes$outcome)
  ) |>
  dplyr::arrange(Modules, outcome, Population) |>
  dplyr::mutate(Population = as.character(Population)) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    Module = Modules,
    Outcome = outcome
  )

write_result_csv(table_2, "table_2_selected_outcomes.csv")

table_2 |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    Outcome = paste0("Module ", Module, ": ", Outcome),
    Outcome = factor(Outcome, levels = unique(Outcome))
  ) |>
  dplyr::select(-Module) |>
  gt::gt(
    groupname_col = "Outcome",
    rowname_col = "Population"
  ) |>
  gt::cols_align(
    align = "center",
    columns = dplyr::all_of(as.character(selected_years))
  ) |>
  gt::tab_style(
    style = gt::cell_text(weight = "bold"),
    locations = list(
      gt::cells_stub(rows = Population %in% c("Women, all", "Men, all", "All adults")),
      gt::cells_body(rows = Population %in% c("Women, all", "Men, all", "All adults"))
    )
  ) |>
  gt::tab_source_note(
    source_note = gt::md(
      paste(
        "Values are model-generated, population-weighted estimates:",
        "mean across simulation replications (95% simulation interval,",
        "2.5th-97.5th percentiles). Education: low (up to basic), medium",
        "(secondary), high (tertiary). QALY loss is per 100,000 adult",
        "person-years and YLL per 100,000 simulated adults. Costs are in",
        "millions of constant 2018 euros; values before 2018 are back-cast by",
        "applying the 2018 cost structure to that year's simulated BMI distribution;",
        "the national total is allocated to sex × education groups by each",
        "group's share of the exposed population (BMI ≥25 kg/m² for high-BMI",
        "costs, BMI ≥30 kg/m² for obesity costs), because GBD has no",
        "education-specific relative risks."
      )
    )
  ) |>
  gt::opt_stylize(
    style = 1,
    color = "gray"
  ) |>
  gt::tab_options(
    table.width = gt::pct(100),
    table.font.size = 10,
    heading.align = "left",
    row_group.font.weight = "bold"
  )
```

### Subgroup analysis: adults aged 20–64

The main outputs of Modules 1 and 2 are repeated for adults aged 20–64 and shown next to the full 20–84 population. Values are computed within each simulation replication and averaged across replications. Obesity-attributable YLL for 20–64 uses PAFs and deaths from that age range only. Costs are reported for ages 20–84 only, because the Borges et al. cost anchor covers all ages and cannot be split by age.

```{r}
#| label: build-subgroup-20-64
#| cache: false

subgroup_years <- reported_years
subgroup_ranges <- list("20–84" = c(20L, 84L), "20–64" = c(20L, 64L))

summarise_age_subgroup <- function(age_label, age_range) {
  living <- simulation_historical |>
    dplyr::filter(
      alive,
      year %in% subgroup_years,
      age >= age_range[1],
      age <= age_range[2]
    ) |>
    dplyr::summarise(
      mean_bmi = stats::weighted.mean(bmi, w = survey_weight, na.rm = TRUE),
      obesity_prevalence = stats::weighted.mean(bmi >= 30, w = survey_weight, na.rm = TRUE),
      .by = c(simulation, year)
    )

  qalys <- qaly_results$individual |>
    dplyr::filter(
      year %in% subgroup_years,
      age >= age_range[1],
      age <= age_range[2]
    ) |>
    dplyr::summarise(
      person_years = sum(survey_weight * person_years, na.rm = TRUE),
      mean_qaly_per_person = sum(qaly_weighted, na.rm = TRUE) / person_years,
      obesity_qaly_loss_per100k = 1e5 * sum(
        qaly_loss_weighted[bmi_category %in% obesity_categories],
        na.rm = TRUE
      ) / person_years,
      .by = c(simulation, year)
    ) |>
    dplyr::select(-person_years)

  # The full 20-84 range reuses the main burden run instead of repeating it.
  subgroup_burden <- if (identical(as.integer(age_range), c(20L, 84L))) {
    burden_results
  } else {
    simeq_calculate_obesity_burden(
      simulation_output   = simulation_historical,
      rr_bmi              = rr_bmi,
      ref_life_expectancy = ref_life_expectancy,
      min_age             = age_range[1],
      max_age             = age_range[2]
    )
  }

  yll <- subgroup_burden$by_year_sim |>
    dplyr::filter(year %in% subgroup_years) |>
    dplyr::summarise(
      obesity_yll_per100k = 1e5 * sum(yll_obesity_attrib_weighted, na.rm = TRUE) /
        sum(N_weighted, na.rm = TRUE),
      .by = c(simulation, year)
    )

  # Mean and 95% simulation interval across replications
  living |>
    dplyr::left_join(qalys, by = c("simulation", "year")) |>
    dplyr::left_join(yll, by = c("simulation", "year")) |>
    tidyr::pivot_longer(
      -c(simulation, year), names_to = "measure", values_to = "value"
    ) |>
    dplyr::summarise(
      mean = mean(value, na.rm = TRUE),
      lower = q_lo(value),
      upper = q_hi(value),
      .by = c(year, measure)
    ) |>
    dplyr::mutate(age_group = age_label, .before = 1L)
}

subgroup_20_64 <- purrr::imap(
  subgroup_ranges,
  \(age_range, age_label) summarise_age_subgroup(age_label, age_range)
) |>
  dplyr::bind_rows() |>
  dplyr::arrange(year, age_group, measure)

write_result_csv(subgroup_20_64, "subgroup_ages_20_64_vs_20_84.csv")
```

## Mortality Scenario: Constant 2024 Mortality {#sec-mortality-scenario}

The base case projects age- and sex-specific background mortality for 2025–2040 with a Lee-Carter model fitted to 1998–2024 (excluding 2020–2021) and anchored to the observed 2024 rates. This scenario repeats the full simulation with the 2024 life table held constant from 2025 to 2040, the assumption used in earlier versions of the model. Everything else is identical: inputs, BMI transitions, education upgrade, entrant pools, random-number seeds, and the treatment of the BMI and education relative risks (recalibrated to the life table each year up to 2024 and held at their 2024 values afterwards). The two runs share the same mortality up to 2024, so 2000 and 2020 should match; differences in 2040 show the effect of the mortality assumption.

```{r}
#| label: run-mortality-scenario-const2024
#| cache: false

# Constant-2024 life table: every year after 2024 repeats the 2024 qx by age
# and sex.
life_table_const2024 <- life_table |>
  dplyr::left_join(
    life_table |>
      dplyr::filter(year == last_observed_life_table_year) |>
      dplyr::select(age, sex, qx_2024 = qx),
    by = c("age", "sex")
  ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(qx = dplyr::if_else(year > last_observed_life_table_year, qx_2024, qx)) |>
  dplyr::select(-qx_2024)

sim_rds_const2024 <- sub(".rds", "_const2024mort.rds", sim_rds, fixed = TRUE)
sim_path_const2024 <- file.path(results_dir, sim_rds_const2024)

# The run is cached; it is read only when its summary has to be recomputed.
if (!file.exists(sim_path_const2024)) {
  simulation_const2024 <- simeq_run_simulation(
    population = population_1998,
    settings = settings_historical,
    life_table = life_table_const2024,
    last_observed_year = last_observed_life_table_year,
    rr_bmi = rr_bmi,
    rr_education = rr_education,
    donor_pool = donor_pool_1998,
    donor_pools = donor_pools_module1,
    entrant_targets = entrant_targets_historical,
    bmi_transition_model = bmi_transition_model,
    bmi_update_method = "percentile",
    bmi_percentile_model = bmi_percentile_model,
    bmi_period = "by_year",
    stochastic_bmi = TRUE,
    education_source = "existing",
    bmi_limits = c(10, 80),
    education_upgrade = education_upgrade
  )
  save_result_rds(simulation_const2024, sim_rds_const2024)
}

# Replication-level outcomes of one run, for the reported years.
summarise_mortality_scenario <- function(sim) {
  # Keep only the reported years: the full 1998-2040 output does not fit in
  # memory once QALYs, YLL and costs are computed on it.
  # 2018 is kept as well: the cost function needs its base-year population.
  sim <- sim[as.integer(sim$year) %in% c(reported_years, 2018L), , drop = FALSE]
  invisible(gc())
  living <- sim |>
    dplyr::filter(alive, year %in% reported_years, age >= 20L, age <= 84L) |>
    dplyr::summarise(
      adults = sum(survey_weight),
      mean_bmi = stats::weighted.mean(bmi, survey_weight, na.rm = TRUE),
      obesity = stats::weighted.mean(bmi >= 30, survey_weight, na.rm = TRUE),
      .by = c(simulation, year)
    )
  deaths <- sim |>
    dplyr::filter(!alive, year %in% reported_years) |>
    dplyr::summarise(deaths = sum(survey_weight), .by = c(simulation, year))

  qalys <- simeq_calculate_qalys(
    simulation_output = sim, min_age = 20L, max_age = 84L,
    reference_bmi_prevalence = reference_bmi_prevalence
  )$individual |>
    dplyr::filter(year %in% reported_years) |>
    dplyr::summarise(
      qaly_loss = sum(qaly_loss_weighted[bmi_category %in% obesity_categories], na.rm = TRUE),
      person_years = sum(survey_weight * person_years, na.rm = TRUE),
      .by = c(simulation, year)
    ) |>
    dplyr::transmute(simulation, year, qaly_loss_per100k = 1e5 * qaly_loss / person_years)

  yll <- simeq_calculate_obesity_burden(
    simulation_output = sim, rr_bmi = rr_bmi,
    ref_life_expectancy = ref_life_expectancy, min_age = 20L, max_age = 84L
  )$by_year_sim |>
    dplyr::filter(year %in% reported_years) |>
    dplyr::summarise(yll = sum(yll_obesity_attrib_weighted, na.rm = TRUE), .by = c(simulation, year))

  costs <- calculate_annual_obesity_costs(
    simulation_output = sim, gbd_rr_matrix = gbd_rr_matrix, costs_dro = costs_2018,
    outcome_mapping = cost_mapping, exclude_disease_groups = c("obesity_overweight", "depression"),
    years = reported_years, exposure = "obesity", bmi_reference = 22,
    weight_col = "survey_weight", base_cost_year = 2018L, unit_cost_annual_growth = 0,
    cpi_2026 = cpi_2026, discount_rate = discount_rate, discount_base_year = 2026L,
    by_simulation = TRUE
  )$totals_by_simulation |>
    dplyr::filter(year %in% reported_years) |>
    dplyr::transmute(simulation, year = as.integer(year), cost_obesity = total_keur_2018_constant / 1000)

  living |>
    dplyr::left_join(deaths, by = c("simulation", "year")) |>
    dplyr::left_join(qalys, by = c("simulation", "year")) |>
    dplyr::left_join(yll, by = c("simulation", "year")) |>
    dplyr::left_join(costs, by = c("simulation", "year")) |>
    dplyr::mutate(yll_per100k = 1e5 * yll / adults) |>
    dplyr::select(-yll)
}

scenario_summary_path <- file.path(
  results_dir, sub(".rds", "_mortality_scenario_summary.rds", sim_rds, fixed = TRUE)
)
if (file.exists(scenario_summary_path)) {
  mortality_scenario_runs <- readRDS(scenario_summary_path)
} else {
  mortality_scenario_lc <- summarise_mortality_scenario(simulation_historical) |>
    dplyr::mutate(scenario = "Lee-Carter (base case)")
  if (!exists("simulation_const2024")) simulation_const2024 <- readRDS(sim_path_const2024)
  mortality_scenario_const <- summarise_mortality_scenario(simulation_const2024) |>
    dplyr::mutate(scenario = "Constant 2024 mortality")
  rm(simulation_const2024); invisible(gc())
  mortality_scenario_runs <- dplyr::bind_rows(mortality_scenario_lc, mortality_scenario_const)
  saveRDS(mortality_scenario_runs, scenario_summary_path)
}

mortality_scenario <- mortality_scenario_runs |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(
    c(adults, mean_bmi, obesity, deaths, qaly_loss_per100k, yll_per100k, cost_obesity),
    names_to = "outcome", values_to = "value"
  ) |>
  dplyr::summarise(mean = mean(value, na.rm = TRUE), lo = q_lo(value), hi = q_hi(value),
                   .by = c(scenario, outcome, year))

write_result_csv(mortality_scenario, "mortality_scenario_const2024_vs_lee_carter.csv")
```

```{r}
mortality_outcome_labels <- c(

)

mortality_outcome_digits <- c(adults = 2, deaths = 1, mean_bmi = 2, obesity = 1,
                              qaly_loss_per100k = 0, yll_per100k = 0, cost_obesity = 1)

mortality_scenario |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    value = mapply(
      function(m, l, h, o) format_interval(m, l, h, digits = mortality_outcome_digits[[o]],
                                           scale = mortality_outcome_scale[[o]]),
      mean, lo, hi, outcome
    ),
    outcome = factor(mortality_outcome_labels[outcome], levels = mortality_outcome_labels)
  ) |>
  dplyr::select(outcome, scenario, year, value) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = year, values_from = value) |>
  dplyr::arrange(outcome, dplyr::desc(scenario == "Lee-Carter (base case)")) |>
  gt::gt(groupname_col = "outcome", rowname_col = "scenario") |>
  gt::opt_stylize(style = 1, color = "gray") |>
  gt::tab_options(table.width = gt::pct(100), table.font.size = 11,
                  row_group.font.weight = "bold")
```

## Supplementary Outputs and Exports

### Master Results Table (CSV)

The chunk below consolidates the headline outputs from Modules 1–3, together with Monte Carlo precision diagnostics and dependent-calibration error metrics, into a single tidy CSV (`paper_i_master_results.csv`) suitable for downstream reporting or a manuscript's results section.

```{r}
#| label: export-paper-i-master-results
#| include: false
#| warning: false
#| message: false

paper_results_file <- file.path(tables_dir, "paper_i_master_results.csv")

master_selected_years <- reported_years

weighted_overall_module1 <- bmi_by_rep |>
  dplyr::group_by(simulation, year) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    mean_bmi = stats::weighted.mean(
      mean_bmi,
      w = weighted_population,
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),
    obesity_prevalence = stats::weighted.mean(
      obesity_prevalence,
      w = weighted_population,
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

module1_overall_results <- weighted_overall_module1 |>
  dplyr::filter(year %in% master_selected_years) |>
  dplyr::group_by(year) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    mean_bmi = mean(mean_bmi, na.rm = TRUE),
    mean_bmi_lo = stats::quantile(
      mean_bmi,
      probs = 0.025,
      na.rm = TRUE,
      names = FALSE
    ),
    mean_bmi_hi = stats::quantile(
      mean_bmi,
      probs = 0.975,
      na.rm = TRUE,
      names = FALSE
    ),
    obesity_prevalence = mean(obesity_prevalence, na.rm = TRUE),
    obesity_prevalence_lo = stats::quantile(
      obesity_prevalence,
      probs = 0.025,
      na.rm = TRUE,
      names = FALSE
    ),
    obesity_prevalence_hi = stats::quantile(
      obesity_prevalence,
      probs = 0.975,
      na.rm = TRUE,
      names = FALSE
    ),
    mean_bmi_mcse = stats::sd(mean_bmi, na.rm = TRUE) / sqrt(dplyr::n()),
    obesity_prevalence_mcse =
      stats::sd(obesity_prevalence, na.rm = TRUE) / sqrt(dplyr::n()),
    mean_bmi_cv_percent =
      100 * stats::sd(mean_bmi, na.rm = TRUE) /
      mean(mean_bmi, na.rm = TRUE),
    obesity_prevalence_cv_percent =
      100 * stats::sd(obesity_prevalence, na.rm = TRUE) /
      mean(obesity_prevalence, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

  ) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(
    cols = dplyr::everything(),
    names_to = "statistic",
    values_to = "value"
  ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    section = "Dependent temporal calibration",
    outcome = "Obesity prevalence",
    year = NA_integer_,
    sex = "overall",
    education_level = "overall",
    unit = "percentage points",
    definition = dplyr::case_when(
      statistic == "obesity_mae_pp" ~
        "Mean absolute error across six sex-by-year comparisons",
      statistic == "obesity_rmse_pp" ~
        "Root mean squared error across six sex-by-year comparisons"
    ),
    statistic = dplyr::recode(
      statistic,
      obesity_mae_pp = "mean absolute error",
      obesity_rmse_pp = "root mean squared error"
    )
  ) |>
  dplyr::select(
    section,
    outcome,
    year,
    sex,
    education_level,
    statistic,
    value,
    unit,
    definition
  )

qaly_master <- qaly_results$by_year |>
  dplyr::group_by(year) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    weighted_person_years = sum(mean_weighted_person_years, na.rm = TRUE),
    total_qalys_weighted = sum(mean_total_qalys_weighted, na.rm = TRUE),
    mean_qaly_per_person = dplyr::if_else(
      weighted_person_years > 0,
      total_qalys_weighted / weighted_person_years,
      NA_real_
    ),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  dplyr::filter(year %in% master_selected_years) |>
  dplyr::transmute(
    section = "Illustrative Portuguese outputs",
    outcome = "Mean annual QALY per person",
    year,
    sex = "overall",
    education_level = "overall",
    statistic = "mean",
    value = mean_qaly_per_person,
    unit = "QALYs per person-year",
    definition = "Weighted total QALYs divided by weighted person-years (decedents count half a year)"
  )

# burden_results$by_year holds per-100k rates only, with no population-size
# column of its own (unlike qaly_results$by_year's mean_weighted_population),
# so the weights for a population-weighted overall mean are computed
# separately from simulation_historical and joined in -- the same approach
# tbl-main-selected-outcomes already uses.
yll_population_weights_master <- simulation_historical |>
  dplyr::filter(
    alive,
    year %in% master_selected_years
  ) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    weighted_population = sum(survey_weight, na.rm = TRUE),
    .by = c(year, sex, education_level)
  )

yll_master <- burden_results$by_year |>
  dplyr::filter(year %in% master_selected_years) |>
  dplyr::left_join(
    yll_population_weights_master,
    by = c("year", "sex", "education_level")
  ) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    yll_per_100k = stats::weighted.mean(
      yll_obesity_per100k,
      w = weighted_population,
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),
    .by = year
  ) |>
  dplyr::transmute(
    section = "Illustrative Portuguese outputs",
    outcome = "Obesity-attributable YLL",
    year,
    sex = "overall",
    education_level = "overall",
    statistic = "mean",
    value = yll_per_100k,
    unit = "per 100,000 simulated adults",
    definition = "Obesity-attributable years of life lost (PAF of the year before death x remaining life expectancy at death)"
  )

# `cost_trajectory` (= annual_costs$totals, built in run-cost-trajectory,
# the annual cost trajectory section) carries `total_keur_2018_constant` in THOUSANDS of euros, so
# the million-euro conversion divides by 1,000 (not 1e6).
# Totals include the direct overweight-and-obesity treatment costs
# (include_direct_costs = TRUE), so nothing is added on top here. The
# interval columns come from by_simulation = TRUE in run-cost-trajectory.
cost_master_selected <- cost_trajectory |>
  dplyr::filter(year %in% master_selected_years)

cost_master <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  cost_master_selected |>
    dplyr::transmute(
      section = "Illustrative Portuguese outputs",
      outcome = "High-BMI-attributable direct healthcare costs",
      year,
      sex = "overall",
      education_level = "overall",
      statistic = "mean",
      value = total_keur_2018_constant / 1000,
      unit = "million constant 2018 euros",
      definition = "Annual high-BMI-attributable cost estimate in constant 2018 prices"
    ),
  cost_master_selected |>
    dplyr::transmute(
      section = "Illustrative Portuguese outputs",
      outcome = "High-BMI-attributable direct healthcare costs",
      year,
      sex = "overall",
      education_level = "overall",
      statistic = "simulation interval lower",
      value = total_keur_2018_constant_lo / 1000,
      unit = "million constant 2018 euros",
      definition = "2.5th percentile across simulation replications"
    ),
  cost_master_selected |>
    dplyr::transmute(
      section = "Illustrative Portuguese outputs",
      outcome = "High-BMI-attributable direct healthcare costs",
      year,
      sex = "overall",
      education_level = "overall",
      statistic = "simulation interval upper",
      value = total_keur_2018_constant_hi / 1000,
      unit = "million constant 2018 euros",
      definition = "97.5th percentile across simulation replications"
    )
)

master_paper_results <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  module1_overall_master,
  module1_stratified_master,
  calibration_master,
  calibration_error_metrics_master,
  qaly_master,
  yll_master,
  cost_master
) |>
  dplyr::arrange(
    section,
    outcome,
    year,
    sex,
    education_level,
    statistic
  )

readr::write_csv(
  master_paper_results,
  paper_results_file,
  na = ""
)

message(
  "Master manuscript-results table written to: ",
  normalizePath(paper_results_file, winslash = "/", mustWork = FALSE)
)
```

### Word-format Supplementary Tables

The headline outcomes table (@tbl-main-selected-outcomes, @sec-headline) is also exported as an editable Word table for manuscript preparation.

```{r}
#| label: export-table-2-word
#| include: false

table_2_word <- flextable::flextable(table_2) |>
  flextable::theme_booktabs() |>
  flextable::font(fontname = "Arial", part = "all") |>
  flextable::fontsize(size = 9, part = "all") |>
  flextable::bold(part = "header") |>
  flextable::bg(bg = "#D9EAF7", part = "header") |>
  flextable::merge_v(j = c("Module", "Outcome")) |>
  flextable::align(j = c("Outcome", "Population"), align = "left", part = "all") |>
  flextable::align(j = as.character(selected_years), align = "center", part = "all") |>
  flextable::valign(valign = "center", part = "all") |>
  flextable::autofit() |>
  flextable::set_table_properties(layout = "autofit", width = 1)

flextable::save_as_docx(
  `Table 2. Selected model-generated outcomes from the Portuguese simeq reference application in 2000, 2020 and 2040 (simulation 1998-2040), by sex and education level. Mean across simulation replications (95% simulation interval).` = table_2_word,
  path = file.path(word_dir, "Table_2_simeq_selected_outcomes.docx")
)
```

## Package Availability

This report was produced with simeq 1.0.1, released at <https://github.com/BertaValente/simeq> under the MIT licence. The release is archived on Zenodo, which gives it a citable DOI. The `data-raw/` and `mortality_lc/` scripts rebuild the model inputs. The National Health Survey microdata (available from INE and INSA on request) and the life tables derived from the Human Mortality Database are not distributed.
